title: A whore of Babylon
html_source:
From the Revelations of St. John the Divine:

Revelations 17.

Revelations, in the New Testament, had many Old Testament characteristics. Much of it retells visions and details of the apocalypse. The Whore of Babylon is a symbolic figure representing the Roman Empire who were about to persecute Christians at the time John wrote it (Sparknotes).

anchor.prefix:
— Yes. 

 Christfox in leather trews, hiding, a runaway in blighted treeforks, from hue and cry. Knowing no vixen, walking lonely in the chase. Women he won to him, tender people,
anchor.suffix: , ladies of justices, bully tapsters' wives. Fox and geese. And in New Place a slack dishonoured body that once was comely, once as sweet, as fresh as cinnamon, now her leaves fall
